rubric.scoring: Preserve the supplied facts and qualifiers in original prose. Compute initial coverage credit as 20 times the sum of case fact weights multiplied by coverage levels (1 complete, 0.5 partial, 0 absent/contradicted), divided by the sum of fact weights. Material contradictions additionally trigger the stated penalty. Do not require every detail twice.

Start at 10. Every claimed experimental quantity must be grounded in an approved numeric record or directly stated source fact, with faithful units and statistic. Permit explicit approximate rounding, simple arithmetic with unchanged meaning, and ordinary bibliography/model-name digits. Apply penalties for unsupported quantities or distorted numeric meanings.

Start at 10. Preserve the baseline identity, metric, aggregation, evidence type and workload population relevant to each claim. Apply penalties for unjustified scope expansion or comparison substitution. Omission of a metric is not itself an unsupported comparison.

Judge whether the introduction gives a specific problem, the reason that problem remains consequential, and a coherent relationship between the proposed contribution and that problem. Full credit does not depend on any fixed paragraph role, novelty slogan, or resemblance to the source.

Judge whether the prose explains how the supplied method produces its intended effect, including the causal link from design choice to outcome and any necessary cost or constraint. Names alone do not establish the mechanism. Do not demand architectural detail absent from the brief.

Judge whether the contribution is supported by an appropriate, scoped result or methodological observation and whether limitations needed to interpret the selected evidence remain visible. Accept selective emphasis. A quantitative claim is useful only with interpretable meaning.

Judge whether the contribution is distinguished from the supplied problem setting or prior approaches without invented priority claims, literature or superiority. Citations, if present, must use provided keys with an appropriate relationship; a fixed citation count is not required.

Judge concise, connected, specific prose, an approximately requested-length self-contained abstract, and three introduction paragraphs. Avoid rewarding verbosity or imposing the original paper wording/organization. Format penalties below apply objectively.

material_fabrication_rule: Flag material fabricated mechanisms, results, datasets, comparisons or deployment evidence independently of the numeric score; such an output cannot count as a passing faithful-paper rewrite. Record the offending claim and supporting fact ID.

fact_coverage.text: The target is general matrix multiplication arising during DNN training, including matrices with uneven dimensions and unstructured zeros. A fixed systolic shape can strand multipliers and preserve useless zero operations.

SIGMA groups a logical row of multipliers into Flexible Dot Product Engines (Flex-DPEs). A Benes distribution fabric supports multicast, and the Forwarding Adder Network (FAN) routes partial sums so independently sized dot products can share the reduction fabric.

A bitmap identifies zero positions and guides placement of useful operands. Multiple Flex-DPEs compose into a Flex-DPU for a GEMM; weight-stationary and input-stationary mappings are evaluated and the better mapping is reported.
fact_coverage.locator: IV.B–E, PDF pp.8–9; VI.B, PDF pp.10–11

fact_coverage.text: Performance comes from a cycle-based analytical model; the systolic baseline uses SCALE-sim. The study uses dimensions/sparsities from GNMT, Transformer, NCF, and DeepBench, and scales each modeled accelerator to 16,384 PEs. Sparse baselines include EIE, SCNN, OuterSPACE, Eyeriss v2, Packed Systolic, and Cambricon-X. These are GEMM comparisons, not full training runs.

The conclusion reports a 5.7× speedup against TPU-like systolic designs on sparse irregular workloads and approximately 3× against the compared sparse accelerators. Sparse accelerators were extended to GEMMs; alternative matrix orientations and sparsity placements were explored.
fact_coverage.locator: VIII, PDF p.13; VI.A, p.10; VI.D, p.12

numeric_facts.meaning: reported sparse irregular GEMM speedup versus modeled TPU-like designs
approximate reported average speedup versus compared sparse designs

fact_coverage.text: Post-layout comparison uses commercial 28 nm technology, 500 MHz, BF16 multiplication and FP32 addition. SIGMA has 65.10 mm² area and 22.33 W power for the compute array. These figures exclude the large SRAMs; the corresponding systolic compute array occupies 47.27 mm² and consumes 12.25 W.

The study reports two GEMMs where Eyeriss v2 is faster because it retains both operands in local SRAM while SIGMA repeats streaming of one operand. Streaming sparsity and bandwidth can limit useful throughput.

fact_coverage.text: Persistent memory is byte-addressable nonvolatile storage reached using ordinary memory instructions. Applications still need crash recovery: data must survive in a permissible order, and volatile DRAM remains in use. An epoch groups persistent stores between ordering points.

WHISPER gathers ten applications spanning direct persistence, transactional libraries, and file-system access. Programs were adapted for recovery and instrumented; workloads include native key-value/database systems, library-backed stores, and PMFS-backed services. Eliza extracts persistent-access traces.

numeric_facts.meaning: suite size, not count of simulated HOPS workloads

fact_coverage.text: Most durable transactions contain between 5 and 50 epochs, although Echo and the N-store TPC-C workload can contain over a hundred. Same-thread epoch conflicts are common; conflicts between threads are uncommon in the measured traces, rather than impossible.

numeric_facts.meaning: common range with explicitly reported exceptions

fact_coverage.text: In the simulated application subset, persistent accesses average 3.54% of memory accesses. Persistent-memory support therefore shares a machine dominated by volatile traffic; this is a workload observation, not a theorem about all PM programs.

numeric_facts.meaning: mean persistent-access fraction in the simulated subset

fact_coverage.text: The Hands-Off Persistence System (HOPS) separates ordering from completion of persistence. ofence ends an epoch without demanding synchronous durability; dfence waits for durability when required, such as transaction completion. Per-thread Persist Buffers retain persistent updates and versions while dependency metadata preserves necessary order.

HOPS is evaluated using gem5 full-system Linux simulation of a four-core out-of-order x86 machine. Each hardware thread has a 32-entry Persist Buffer, with background flushing triggered at 16 entries. A subset of the suite runs to completion.

Against x86-64 clwb plus sfence with durability reached at NVM, HOPS without persistent write queues reports a 24.3% performance improvement. It also outperforms the x86-64 persistent-write-queue configuration by 10%. The ideal comparison ignores ordering and is not crash-consistent.

numeric_facts.meaning: reported performance improvement, HOPS(NVM) versus x86-64(NVM)
reported improvement of HOPS without PWQ versus x86-64 with PWQ

fact_coverage.text: This is an evaluation of a deployed Tensor Processing Unit (TPU) for datacenter neural-network inference. Six production models, comprising MLP, CNN, and LSTM families, represent 95% of the provider’s inference demand at the time. The compared contemporary platforms are Intel Haswell and Nvidia K80.
fact_coverage.locator: Table1, author PDF p.2; 3, PDF p.5

numeric_facts.meaning: provider inference demand represented by the selected workload at the time

fact_coverage.text: The host-controlled coprocessor uses a dense systolic matrix unit with 65,536 multiply-accumulate units for 8-bit integer operands. Software manages the Unified Buffer; the accelerator uses a simple deterministic execution scheme and communicates with a host over PCIe. It targets inference rather than training.

Peak throughput is 92 trillion operations per second; the Unified Buffer has 24 MiB, supplemented by 4 MiB of accumulators. Peak arithmetic rate is not sustained workload throughput. Dense hardware lacks dedicated sparse-operation support.

Measured comparisons enforce application response-time limits and include host interaction overhead. For MLP0, the tail-latency limit is 7 ms at the 99th percentile. Larger batches can increase throughput while violating that service constraint. CPU and GPU results use floating point; TPU inference is quantized, so this is not an equal-datapath comparison.
fact_coverage.locator: 4, Table4 and Table6, PDF p.8; 8, PDF p.13

fact_coverage.text: Table6 reports TPU throughput relative to Haswell of 14.5× geometric mean and 29.2× production-weighted mean. Relative to K80, the corresponding TPU ratios are 13.2× and 15.3×. Both summaries include host overhead; weighted and geometric averages differ.

For complete-server performance per watt, TPU is reported as 17–34× Haswell and 14–16× K80, depending on averaging. The higher incremental ratios subtract host-server power. Energy efficiency is a disclosed proxy; negotiated purchase prices and total ownership cost are not disclosed.

Roofline and counter analysis identify memory limits in the MLP/LSTM workloads; low utilization can coexist with high relative throughput. On CNN0 at 10% offered load, TPU consumes 88% of its full-load power, revealing weak energy proportionality.
fact_coverage.locator: 4, PDF pp.6–8; 6 and Fig.10, PDF pp.10–11

numeric_facts.meaning: fraction of full-load TPU power at that load

fact_coverage.text: An accelerator’s dataflow fixes the scheduling and spatial placement of tensor computations. Layer dimensions, data reuse, buffering, communication bandwidth, and available parallelism interact, making a stationary-data label insufficient as a full mapping description.

MAESTRO expresses dataflow through TemporalMap, SpatialMap, and Cluster directives. Analysis derives tensor reuse and communication opportunities at each hierarchy level, then estimates runtime, activity counts, energy, buffer requirements, and utilization from the workload, mapping, and hardware inputs.

Reuse opportunities require matching hardware support, such as multicast, reductions, and suitable buffers. The energy calculation combines activity counts with component energy estimates; design-space experiments also use synthesized component area/power costs. More PEs or more buffering alone need not improve a bandwidth-constrained design.
fact_coverage.locator: Table2, PDF p.7; 4.2–4.4, PDF p.9; 5 and 5.2, PDF pp.10–12

fact_coverage.text: Runtime validation compares predictions with a 64-PE MAERI RTL simulation on VGG16 and reported Eyeriss runtimes on AlexNet. Average absolute runtime error is within 3.9% for those comparisons; this is not a demonstrated bound for all dataflows or an energy-error result.

numeric_facts.meaning: reported average absolute runtime error on the stated validation

fact_coverage.text: The study evaluates five dataflow styles on operators from five DNN models and observes that preferred mappings change with operator characteristics. Adaptive choices show potential runtime and energy reductions of 37% and 10% in that modeled case study, rather than a measured chip improvement.

numeric_facts.meaning: modeled potential runtime reduction with adaptive dataflow
modeled potential energy reduction with adaptive dataflow

fact_coverage.text: The hardware search varies PE count, local buffer, shared buffer, and NoC bandwidth under area and power constraints. In the KC-P/VGG16-CONV2 run, Figure13(c) lists 3,936,256 explored points, 175,861 valid points, and 12.20 minutes. The search skips infeasible regions using cost lower bounds; explored points must not be described as that many full simulations.

numeric_facts.meaning: explored design-space size for KC-P/VGG16-CONV2 only
reported execution time for that run

fact_coverage.text: The search experiments use an Intel i7-8700K host with 32 GB memory, synthesized 28 nm building-block costs, and constraints of 16 mm² and 450 mW. These are experimental search settings, not MAESTRO hardware overhead.

MAESTRO is an analytical exploration tool. Future plans include automatic dataflow tuning and RTL generation; they are not completed capabilities demonstrated by this paper. The dataflow comparison abstracts implementation differences rather than proving one manufactured accelerator superior.

penalty_rules.trigger: A factual claim materially contradicts the supplied method, evaluation or result. Missing a fact is handled only by coverage credit, not this penalty.
An experimental result, hardware cost, workload size or other material quantitative claim has no support in the brief or approved numeric inventory. Count a repeated same claim only once.
A supported value is assigned the wrong unit, denominator, precision, aggregation, or interpretation, including an unjustified conversion between performance gain and runtime reduction.
A comparative claim substitutes or drops a baseline or baseline condition essential to its interpretation.

A claim promotes kernel results to end-to-end execution, simulation/modeling to measured deployment, a sampled workload to universal behavior, a mean to a worst-case bound, or a hypothetical capability to a delivered result.
The output adds a material architectural mechanism, interface, capability or guarantee not supplied by the brief.
An invented citation, unsupported attribution to cited work, or unsupported first/best/only priority claim is used as positioning.
Abstract word count is below 175 or above 235; the requested 180–230 range receives a five-word tolerance because the task says about. Exclude its heading.
Introduction has other than exactly three prose paragraphs. Exclude its heading and separate bibliography records; bullet lists do not satisfy the prose-paragraph requirement.

score_contract.quality_metric_raw_scores: For argument, mechanism, evidence, positioning and economy, grader assigns raw score in [0, metric weight]. For fact_fidelity use the coverage formula; unsupported_numbers and baselines_scope start at full weight.
score_contract.penalty_application: Apply each distinct claim to the single most specific applicable penalty rule; do not double-penalize the same underlying error. Deduct penalties within the assigned metric, respecting both each rule cap and the metric weight, and clamp the result to [0,weight]. Penalties are not deducted again from the final total. Sum final metric scores.
score_contract.adjudication_evidence: For every nonzero penalty provide one minimal output quotation, applicable fact IDs if any, and a concise reason. Cite source locators from the key for disputed factual assessments. Do not include an intended rewrite.
score_contract.fatal_fabrication: Set true for a fabricated central mechanism, material result, workload, baseline or deployment claim. This independently prevents declaring a faithful rewrite pass; keep the numeric score for diagnosis.
score_contract.threshold_note: No validated pass threshold is assumed by this small evaluation; report paired scores and failure flags instead of tuning a threshold on held-out outcomes.

expected_grader_output.metric_raw_scores: object mapping each stable metric_id to a number in [0,weight]
expected_grader_output.penalties: array of {rule_id:string, count:nonnegative integer, evidence:string, fact_ids:string[]}
expected_grader_output.rationale: string; concise evidence-based assessment, not an intended answer

source_overlap_policy.access: Constructor and evaluator only; never pass source fulltext, overlap source spans, or source-manifest to writers.
source_overlap_policy.interpretation: An exact-overlap diagnostic is reported independently of scientific merit. Exclude bibliography records, required terminology, and source titles from prose-overlap counts. Shared generic prose spans require human review, not automatic accusation. No model-pretraining-unseen claim is warranted.
